questions.question: What happened when Moses threw his staff on the ground the first time God instructed him?
options: It turned into a bird.
It stayed a staff.
It turned into a snake.
It disappeared.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states: 'Wa i ponsa pansi, ya penduka inyoka' (He threw it down, it turned into a snake).

questions.question: What was Moses' main concern when God told him to go speak to the people?
options: He was afraid of Pharaoh.
He felt he was not good at speaking.
He didn't believe the people would listen.
He didn't want to leave Jethro.
questions.explanation: Verse 10: 'E, Nkosi, a ngi siye umuntu o namazwi... ngi butuntu emlonyeni, ngi butuntu na solimini' (Oh, Lord, I am not a man of words... I am slow of speech and slow of tongue).

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the primary reason God gave Moses these miraculous signs?
options: To impress Pharaoh with his power.
To show Moses he was the true God.
So the people would believe that the Lord had appeared to Moses.
To train Moses as a magician.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says: 'Ukuba ba ze ba kolwe ukuti, uJehova... u bonakele kuwe' (So that they may believe that the Lord... has appeared to you). Verse 8 reinforces this: 'uma be nga kolwa uwe... ba ya kukolwa izwi lesibonakaliso samuva' (if they do not believe you... they will believe the word of the latter sign).

questions.question: What did Zipporah do when the Lord sought to kill Moses at the lodging place?
options: She prayed to the Lord.
She argued with Moses.
She took a sharp stone and circumcised her son.
She ran away in fear.
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states: 'uZipora wa tabata itye elibukali, wa nguma ijwabu lendodana yake' (Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son).

questions.question: What was Aaron's role in helping Moses communicate with the people?
options: He would perform all the miracles himself.
He would be Moses' mouth, speaking for him to the people.
He would gather food for their journey.
He would lead the people into Egypt.
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clarifies: 'U ya ku kukulumela ebantwini, a be umlomo kuwe' (He shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be a mouth for you).
